units.en: ⟦0⟧ is a minor power located on the Iberian Peninsula, bordering ⟦1⟧ to the west, ⟦2⟧ to the northeast, the Mediterranean Sea around the south to the west, the Atlantic Ocean to the north and northwest, and the ⟦3⟧ by its colonial holding of Gibraltar. Republican Spain also borders France via Spain's colonial holdings in Spanish Africa, Rio de Oro, and Equatorial Guinea. When used with the 11th of November rule(which can be found in the custom game rules), ⟦4⟧ is known as ⟦5⟧. ⟦6⟧ borders ⟦7⟧ in the south instead of ⟦8⟧, ⟦9⟧ in the east, ⟦10⟧ in the northeast and ⟦11⟧ in the west. It has sea access in the north and south.

When the dictatorship of Primo de Rivera came to an end on January 28, 1930, Spain faced an unparalleled political dilemma. Groups across all ideologies disputed the nation's fate, divided between monarchists and republicans. King Alfonso XIII called a national referendum so that Spaniards could decide between a constitutional monarchy and a republic by 1931. Although the monarchists won in rural areas, the republicans or the "Popular Front" won overwhelmingly in cities and industrial centers. The republican success in the urban areas convinced Alfonso XIII to abdicate and led to the establishment of the Second Spanish Republic under the Populat Front. The Republic itself would be a major experiment for democracy in Spain to see how it would operate without the Bourbon monarchy. However, the Republic faces political and military instability from right-wing elements opposed to democracy, resulting in at least one failed coup attempt in 1932 by General José Sanjurjo, known as the Sanjurjada. Furthermore, the nation struggled with deep political divisions from not only the right-wing but also the left-wing as well from groups like the Carlists, the Falangists and the CNI-FAI. The government sought to keep the political balance and work with republican elements from the left and the right to maintain stability. But it would not be enough as political instability grew even further throughout the early to mid 1930s.

With the nation on the brink of civil war, the Second Spanish Republic faced multiple coup attempts; the most famous being the "Revolution" of Asturias in 1934 led by the Spanish Socialist Workers Party and the Communist Party of Spain that left more than 20,000 dead and saw Francisco Franco named as a hero of the Republic for quelling the uprising, and more than 2,500 political assassinations throughout the nation during its six years of life. In 1936, the government of Niceto Alcalá-Zamora gave way to that of Manuel Azaña in elections marked by corruption, which led the Popular Front to victory.
Main article: Republican Spanish national focus tree
⟦0⟧ gets a unique focus tree as with the La Résistance expansion. Without the expansion, it utilizes the ⟦1⟧ instead.

The Republican Spanish national focus tree can be divided into 12 sections. 1 pre civil war branch leading into 3 main branches and 2 shared branches. A post civil war sub-branch can be split from each of these branches. The post civil war Communist Branch can be divided into 2 separate sub branches:

This pre-Spanish Civil War branch gives Republican Spain army battalions when the Civil War begins as well as disadvantages to the ⟦0⟧. It also gives political power. These focuses take longer than the Nationalist pre-war focuses so it is in the player's best interest to extend the pre-civil war preparations until all the focuses are complete (The final focus will start the civil war).
Regional Defense Council of Aragon Branch

The ⟦0⟧ branch of the focus tree allows beneficial modifiers to the ⟦1⟧ national spirit as well as the special ⟦2⟧ economy law and "Council" government advisors. This branch also creates an Anarchist civil war in ⟦3⟧ which may lead to its annexation and coring of all its core states.

Once the Spanish Civil War is over, ⟦0⟧ may rebuild its economy in preparation for future wars. This branch also gives bonuses to war goal justification time and decisions to create anarchist uprisings in foreign nations as well as the coring of states with high compliance.
International Brigades/Seize the Gold Reserves Branch

This branch is shared between ⟦0⟧ and ⟦1⟧. It allows a weekly manpower boost during the civil war, the seizure of gold reserves for factory output and factories and will lead to another front against the rival ideology within the Republican side of the Civil War. It is required in order to progress through the focus tree.
Once the Civil War is over, Spain can take the ⟦0⟧ focus in order to progress to the rest of the post civil war focuses. The other two focuses give bonuses to the navy.

The ⟦0⟧ Branch of the focus tree splits into two sections. The left path allows the creation of a ⟦1⟧ alliance against the ⟦2⟧ and the creation of ⟦3⟧. This allows the ability to take the focuses shared with the ⟦4⟧ and the ⟦5⟧. The right path allows the alliance with the ⟦6⟧ and the creation of ⟦7⟧. This allows the ability to take the focuses shared with the ⟦8⟧ and the ⟦9⟧. The center of the branch is shared with both paths and allows bonuses in the industry. The Focus ⟦10⟧ may be taken by the ⟦11⟧ if they take the ⟦12⟧ focus.

This post civil war sub-branch allows ⟦0⟧ to recover from the Spanish Civil War, make an alliance with other ⟦1⟧ nations not in Asia, and get war goals against every European ⟦2⟧ nation, ⟦3⟧ and the ⟦4⟧.

This post civil war sub-branch allows ⟦0⟧ to try to increase its autonomy if it is a puppet of the ⟦1⟧, gain war goals on ⟦2⟧, ⟦3⟧ and all other nations who sent volunteers to the ⟦4⟧ side. This sub-branch is also shared with ⟦5⟧ if they take the ⟦6⟧ focus and may be done before the civil war is over this way.

This branch is shared between the ⟦0⟧ and the ⟦1⟧. It seeks aid from the ⟦2⟧ for the civil war and in return, Spain will become a puppet under them. It also creates a third faction in the civil war from the ⟦3⟧.
This post civil war sub-branch further increases military development if the Spain is still in a faction with the ⟦0⟧.

The ⟦0⟧ branch allows ⟦1⟧ to increase ⟦2⟧ and military strength. It also asks ⟦3⟧'s help in lend lease. Spain may ⟦4⟧ which leads to independence from the ⟦5⟧ and allows Spain to stay ⟦6⟧. Spain may also allow ⟦7⟧ which will allow Spain to become ⟦8⟧ and take the ⟦9⟧ and the ⟦10⟧ in the ⟦11⟧ side of the focus tree.

This post civil war branch allows ⟦0⟧ to declare war for independence against the ⟦1⟧ with the aid of either the ⟦2⟧ nations or ⟦3⟧ and ⟦4⟧. It also increases military capability and allows Spain to join in the war against the ⟦5⟧ majors.

Spain lies in Southwestern Europe, with most of its land being on the Iberian peninsula. 1930s Spain also comprises the Balearic Islands and African territory and Islands. Parts of North Africa, namely the Rio de Oro region of modern-day Morocco, Western Sahara, Equatorial Guinea, and the Canary Islands off the coast of Northwest Africa are owned and controlled by Spain.

Spain is dominated by mountainous and hilly terrain, and mainland Spain is very uneven, with 45 percent of it being covered by the Meseta Plateau. The plateau is rarely flat, with many uneven hills, mountains, and highlands. Spain contains many significant mountain ranges including the Baetic Mountains in the south, the Central and Iberian Chain in the center, and Cantabrian and Pyrenees Mountain ranges in the northwest and northeast respectively. There is also the fertile Andalusian Plain and other basins. There are many large coastal plains, with bays, coves, and sandy beaches. Along the Bay of Biscay, there are large coastal rugged cliffs. The Strait of Gibraltar separates Spain and Europe from Africa, specifically Morocco, with the closest points being only 13 km apart. Finally, mainland Spain contains over 1,500 rivers of which are mostly small. Significant rivers are the Duero, Ebro and Guadalquivir.

Spain shares a long border with its neighbor ⟦0⟧ which makes up the rest of the Iberian peninsular. It borders ⟦1⟧ in the north, with the tall Pyrenees mountain range making a natural border between the two nations and in the south through their African colonies. Spain also borders ⟦2⟧ in the south with British-controlled Gibraltar.
Spain has multiple important borders to bodies of water, such as the Mediterranean Sea, Strait of Gibraltar, Atlantic Ocean, and the Bay of Biscay.

In 1936, the Second Spanish Republic is riven by internal divisions that prove to be increasingly intractable. As such, a civil war is inevitable and the player can only choose between supporting either the ⟦0⟧ or the Republicans. Specifically, a countdown will commence after the scheduled elections in February 1936, and the civil war will break out once the timer expires. It is in the interest of the Republican player to delay the civil war as long as possible via decisions to gather the maximum possible strength to fight against the Nationalists.
